intent: Bring phone_focus_mode/dns_enforcer.sh under the 250-line cap by moving its iptables chain machinery into a sibling script, and give that code its first working test.
scope: phone_focus_mode/deploy.sh — both per-file lists grown by one entry
changes: Moved ensure_chain, trusted_dot_ips, fill_chain_v4, fill_chain_v6, expected_rule_count, chain_intact and enforce_iptables into dns_iptables.sh, a sibling of the entry script rather than a lib/ member: lib/ does not exist on the phone and deploy.sh copies these files flat into $REMOTE_DIR.

Placed the source line by hand after the existing config.sh line. extract_shell_functions.py refuses to anchor in a #!/system/bin/sh script, and when it refuses it still writes the library but does NOT remove the functions from the source, so a naive run leaves them defined twice. The excision was done separately and confirmed by hash.

Added dns_iptables.sh to BOTH deploy.sh lists — the adb_cmd push staging list and the adb_root cp install list — matching how tether_iptables.sh is handled. It is correctly absent from the chmod 755 line, since a sourced library needs read, not execute.

Deleted test_dns_enforcer.sh. Its six assertions targeted extract_ping_ip, extract_package_uid and append_unique_line, none of which dns_enforcer.sh has ever defined; it died at its source line and had never run a single assertion since the commit that added it.

Wrote test_dns_iptables.sh (20 assertions over all seven moved functions) in the staging style test_tether_enforcer.sh proves works, with the shared staging and stubs in dns_iptables_harness.sh so both files stay under the cap.

verification.evidence: 20 passed, 0 failed, covering expected_rule_count (5 cases), trusted_dot_ips (4), ensure_chain (2), fill_chain_v4/v6 (3), chain_intact (3) and enforce_iptables (3).

verification.command: mutation: expected_rule_count drops the trusted-resolver tally (n+1 -> n+0)
verification.evidence: 'FAIL: adds one ACCEPT per trusted v4 resolver address (want 7, got 6)' — the test catches the undercount that the function's own comment warns causes a rebuild every DNS_CHECK_INTERVAL seconds.

verification.command: mutation: fill_chain_v4 moves the trusted ACCEPT loop after the blanket REJECT
verification.evidence: 'FAIL: puts the trusted-resolver ACCEPT before the blanket REJECT (want ACCEPT, got REJECT)' — first-match ordering is enforced, not assumed.

verification.command: mutation: expected_rule_count counts 3 rules per DoH IP instead of 4
verification.evidence: 6 of the 20 assertions fail. Restoring the file returns 20 passed, 0 failed, so the suite is non-vacuous.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/verify_shell_split.sh HEAD phone_focus_mode/dns_enforcer.sh phone_focus_mode/dns_enforcer.sh phone_focus_mode/dns_iptables.sh
sh dns_enforcer.sh with main() disabled, then command -v each function
verification.evidence: All 11 probed functions resolve (the 7 moved plus log, rotate_log, acquire_lock, ensure_private_dns_off), proving the new source line loads the sibling at runtime and not merely at lint time.

verification.command: shellcheck on all four changed shell files
verification.evidence: Clean, each standing alone, with zero suppressions. Two SC2016 findings were resolved structurally — a [$] character class in the sed pattern and a quoted heredoc prelude — rather than disabled.
23 files over the cap before, 22 after. dns_enforcer.sh 171, dns_iptables.sh 170, test 197, harness 133 — all under.

risks: UNVERIFIED ON THE PHONE. No deploy has run, by explicit instruction. If DNS enforcement misbehaves after the next deploy, dns_iptables.sh reaching the device is the first thing to check — the two deploy.sh list entries are what carry it.

The iptables stub models only the subset of the interface these functions touch (-L/-N/-F/-A/-I/-D/-C/-S). A real iptables failure mode outside that subset, such as a locking error, is not represented.
tether_enforcer.sh remains unverified on the device from the previous session, so two enforcer splits are now in flight at once.
rollback: git revert the commit; dns_enforcer.sh returns to 325 lines, dns_iptables.sh and both new test files disappear, and the two deploy.sh entries are removed together with the code they carry.

After rollback, run sh -n phone_focus_mode/dns_enforcer.sh and confirm the file no longer sources dns_iptables.sh, then grep deploy.sh for dns_iptables to confirm zero hits — a stale cp line pointing at a file that is no longer staged is the failure this ordering prevents.
